decisions.reason: A bleaching tray blank presented on its own page fits the firm's core dental thermoforming range, carries little cost, and with large-firm slack there is no shortfall that would prompt search for other uses.
A PETG thermoforming blank is a staple consumable that complements the established blank portfolio and likely meets aspirations, so dropping it makes little sense.
The UV-curing lacquer is only mentioned on the website, so its evidence is weaker, but as a cheap add-on consumable it can be carried with organisational slack while results stay uncertain.
The intraoral contrast spray has its own page and supports the growing intraoral scanning market, so expected performance is near aspiration and it should be kept.
The custom earmold line is only mentioned and lies in a more peripheral audiology segment, but slack allows the firm to give it time before any problemistic search.
Custom hearing protection earmolds are less visible and less certain, but they share processes with product E, so carrying them is cheap and an early drop is not warranted.
